decision: KEEP pinned esbuild 0.28.2 with Node ESM orchestration; FIX compiled-input byte binding and reject guidance-source drift during the browser build.
constraints: Offline component includes validators and Unicode helper without a package loader, CDN or schema compiler at runtime.
Preserve SDK admission and withdrawal; browser and installed-product acceptance are separate gates.
Fresh compilation, closed bundled input set, exact consumed-byte hashes and licenses; guidance captured before compilation and checked after compilation/bundling. No competing SDK or server changes.

alternatives.assessment: Retained: built-in CommonJS/ESM conversion, browser resolution, write:false, onLoad byte supply and dependency metadata support this closed twelve-input ESM artifact. One local loader callback captures the same bytes used for manifest hashes; no third-party bundler plugin. Executed drift cases support the decision, not a speed ranking.

alternatives.technology: JavaScript / Rollup with CommonJS and node-resolve plugins
alternatives.assessment: Credible ESM bundling and tree shaking. Official CommonJS documentation describes the added conversion plugin. This component needs no plugin customization or chunking; esbuild supplies its conversion and resolution in one pinned tool.

Credible Rust implementation with Rollup-compatible plugin APIs, including load hooks. Current official plugin documentation was accessible in this review. It can express this boundary; no required Rollup plugin integration or measured resource advantage establishes a material migration benefit for this single fixed ESM graph. Not installed or benchmarked.

alternatives.technology: AJV standalone ESM and native unbundled modules
alternatives.assessment: Standalone ESM exports are available; helper references still need resolution. A separate validator format adds a parity surface; bundling the same generated code preserves one admission implementation.

limits: Node data-URL import and structural DOM tests do not qualify browsers, accessibility, CSP deployment, customer installation or hardware.

Manifest hashes exact captured compiled runtime inputs and output artifacts. It remains unsigned, not a full source/toolchain attestation or P19 acceptance. Source drift comparisons require a trusted, exclusively owned build workspace; transient edits reverted between checks are not detected.
ES2022 syntax does not polyfill APIs: strict ingress needs Fetch streams, structuredClone, TextDecoder and JSON.parse reviver context. Actual browsers require validation.
Local byte reproduction is not cross-platform reproducibility or hard-real-time evidence.
No weapon integration, actuation, MLS/CNSA qualification, DDS/Link16 interoperability or five-nines claim.
